limitations: Bounded randomized agreement with a saved solver is not proof of semantic completeness.
rule: Four square panels sit inside a frame. Panel 1 has a wall line and a separate dot. Panel 4 is filled as follows: the dot's side of the wall copies panel 2's pattern, and the other side copies panel 3's pattern. Wall cells show panel 2's colour where panel 2 is not fill, and panel 3's cell otherwise.
scope: Four square panels route two patterns through the two regions of an 8-connected wall, selected by a separate dot. The wall overlays panel 2 over panel 3. Random palette, wall families and motif mixtures support panel sides 4..6 (total widths 21..29).
constraints: Read full source, canonical fixtures and saved transform; adjudicated independent Opus audit
Exclude scenes whose result equals either unconditional overlay, so ignoring the wall/dot cannot solve them
Optional wall_evidence requires both priority and fallback branches; half of unconstrained calls request it
Removed arbitrary two-thirds pattern density cap; actual fill-colour dominance still enforced, including 24 dense 4x4 ring scenes
Validate typed colours/geometry and reject invalid fixed walls/dots across all feasible sizes before retries
120 targeted cases: all defeat both overlays; 97 demonstrate priority and 107 fallback; 93 walls are not straight; 40 scenes at each panel side 4/5/6
Independent component extraction and region routing reproduce output exactly; canonical reconstruction and 1000 independent seeds passed
known_limitations: Four square panels limit panel side to six within the ARC 30-cell grid bound
Wall families are straight, diagonal, L-corner or monotone edge-to-edge paths; arbitrary closed regions and nonmonotone walls are not sampled
Motif mixture includes fixed-shape parametric motifs alongside fresh random patterns; not every motif fits every requested geometry
Original panel side five; sides four/six are labelled synthetic extensions
billing: Claude Max CLI; API credentials excluded; no API fallback

authored_constraints: frame, fill, line, panel-2 and panel-3 colours are pairwise distinct
the wall is 8-connected and splits panel 1 into exactly two 4-connected regions, each of at least 2 cells
the dot is not 8-adjacent to the wall, so it forms a separate, smaller component
the fill colour is strictly the most common colour across panels 1-3
the dot region contains at least one panel-2 pattern cell, and the other region contains at least one panel-3 pattern cell
pattern2 differs from pattern3; each pattern has 3..floor(2N^2/3) cells
frame colour appears at (0,0) and divider columns are the only full frame-colour columns inside the grid
explicit argument combinations that are impossible raise ValueError instead of looping or being silently ignored
